notes.text: Psalm . In singing Psalm 27, God’s people have a way to express confidence in him and to respond to challenging life situations. The psalm describes a faithful person attacked by those who would destroy him. One who can trust God in those circumstances can trust him in other situations as well.

The terms fear and be afraid contrast with be confident. The faithful must learn to base their confidence on God’s ever-present protection (light, salvation, stronghold). This confidence grows through experiences of deliverance (as v. 2 shows).
dwell in the house of the Lord. Compare 23:6. God’s beauty is what the faithful yearn to gaze upon (that is, to view with admiration and affection) as they seek him in worship (see 27:13).
God addresses his words, Seek my face, to more than one person. The singer responds to the invitation. The seeking is done in the sanctuary (see. v. 4).
The goodness of the Lord is probably his gracious character, as revealed by his actions (Ex. 33:19; 34:6–7). On the land of the living see Isa. 38:11; Jer. 11:19.
To wait for the Lord is to look to him with dependence and trust, not passivity. This enables one to be strong and courageous (see Deut. 31:6).
